column4: a shallow checkout read as full makes every ancestry answer a maybe, and the walk grades itself on a truncated history instead of saying so
the walk must ACT on shallowness, not merely observe it: a shallow checkout read as full grades the release on a truncated history and hands down the verdict green instead of failing loud

exec.CommandContext KILLS git on cancel and a killed child is an ordinary ExitError, so reading the exit status first swallows a Ctrl-C into "this commit never landed" — a wrong answer about which commits a release counts, returned with a nil error

cat-file --batch-check answers "<sha> missing" for an object the repository does not hold, so trusting the line without checking it says `commit` claims a sha that is not there and the footprint places a commit that never landed
the lint rules are the fleet's only gate on commit subjects; a dropped rule is invisible until every repo has history it now refuses

the fail-loud gate is the ONLY guard left on an unread range (t-pysg replaced the per-arm refusals with it): without it a walk missing a `:boom:` pull retags a v1.0.0 draft down to v0.1.1 and a none verdict deletes the rolling draft, both at a green exit, on the very reading the walk just said it could not trust (t-441z)
glyph never publishes and never tags: writes are draft-only so a human is always the one who cuts the tag, and that is the whole safety net behind the direct git-cliff flip

FirstParentLog returns FEWER than n commits near the root by contract, and the loop after this indexes mains[i] by the LISTING length — so on any repository whose main is shorter than the pull that landed on it (every first release) a rebase-merge PANICS

with nothing left for an alignment to answer about — a pull that listed no commits, or a merge-button listing ancestry already placed whole — the canonical commit may be a sha this checkout does not hold, so falling through turns "there was nothing to align" into an exit-4 git error mid-walk

a listing is not all-verbatim or all-rewritten: a stacked pull carries its base pull's merge-button-landed commits beside its own rebased ones, and stopping at the first commit placed by ancestry left every rewritten one ungoverned by the range — measured minor out of work released a tag ago, exit 0, no warning, notes citing pre-rebase shas main does not contain (t-7h15)

a rebase does not replay the base-merge commit that "merge main into the branch" leaves, and GitHub permits rebase-merge over one — so letting it hold a position in the alignment window makes the length wrong and abandons the mapping WHOLE, taking with it every commit that could have been placed (t-7h15)

core.hooksPath relocates a repository's hooks and the family's older repos point it at a tracked scripts/hooks, so a doctor that reads .git/hooks inspects a file git never runs — and reports a clean bill of health over the stale hook in the directory git actually uses

git cleans an EDITED message (strip: comments out, cut at the scissors line) and a `-m`/`-F` one only of whitespace, so a hook that assumes the editor ran drops lines git records — the hook blessing a subject CI then rejects, measured in both directions

githooks(5) guarantees only the GIT_EDITOR=":" side: with core.editor or $EDITOR supplying the editor git leaves GIT_EDITOR UNSET in the hook (measured), so reading unset as "no editor" puts those developers on the whitespace branch, where the editor template is never stripped and every commit is malformed-subject at the hook

git trims what ITS isspace calls space — space, tab, CR — so a port that leaves the CR out disagrees with git on every CRLF message it is handed, and the hand-written cases all pass while 82 of 882 generated ones do not

git drops a comment line only at column 0, so treating an indented one as a comment deletes a line git records — and deleting it closes the blank-line gap that makes the NON-BREAKING: below it a trailer, turning a clean commit into undeclared-removal in CI alone

git matches its scissors line at the start of a line and nowhere else, so an unanchored match cuts at text git keeps — and everything below a stray cut line, footers included, disappears from the hook view of a message CI reads whole

bite acts on Go diffs and the smoke reads no YAML, so without the dist-gate job a reusable/action/goreleaser fix ships with zero tests again — the measured pre-gate state (t-5dbh), restored by deleting the one step that runs the gate. The job's checkout stays on purpose: a patch deleting the whole job must carry the dependabot-owned checkout SHA in its deleted lines, and then stops applying on every SHA bump (t-7zy2 — glyph#88/#89/#90 all went red that way)

restore "exactly one of app/binary" and the live-fire range can no longer call this reusable at all, so it goes back to firing a hand copy that drifted three glyph releases behind the workflows around it (t-kcm4)

drop one macOS step's artefact condition and it runs on the ubuntu runner a verdict-only caller lands on — invisible to every artefact-shipping caller, red only in the one repo whose job is to notice breakage first
the retired token quietly lints clean again and two grammars re-enter new history — the debt v1.0.0 exists to end, reopened invisibly because bots are lint-exempt and no human notices a pass

a single-parent commit whose subject merely opens with "Merge " or an unquoted "Revert " slips past lint and the version fold on every parents-aware path — the gate is silently off for exactly the sentences developers write about merging and reverting

a change that reached main twice — its original sha landed by another pull, or its patch already upstream of the rebase — must keep the landing git states: re-pointing the entry at the copy this pull wrote loses the released landing, and when the two straddle the base tag the range counts the change again, t-8xsb one shape over (t-nsww)

the exit-code contract has three full prose homes and the compiler sees none of them, so a row deleted from one is invisible while every remaining row stays correct — which is how the copies got out of step in the first place: README carries the exit-4 refusal clause today and DESIGN and the glossary did not

lint.yml's jq is the fleet's only machine test for a convention violation and jq matching nothing exits 1 into a guard that tolerates it, so a stale integer is silent in both directions — every real violation loses its commit-format hint and every infra failure can gain one — and a membership-only check passes it, because the stale integer is itself a real contract code

exit 4 stopped meaning only I/O the day the release command began returning it for an incomplete walk (t-pysg) and for the published floor — deliberate refusals with nothing broken underneath — so a copy that says only API/git/IO tells the next author a refusal needs a new integer, and a new integer in a frozen machine API is a breaking change every fleet repo's lint gate branches on

one machine format must have ONE flag name: --ndjson never emitted NDJSON — printCompact writes a single object — and the split cost every caller a memorised spelling per subcommand, measured as version --json and bump --ndjson BOTH exiting 2 with unknown flag; enumerating the flag from the command tree is what makes a third spelling fail here instead of in a caller's shell

pflag reports Changed as true for an explicit --json=false, so reading the machine flag by MENTION hands JSON to the caller who just declined it — and it compiles, because an unread package-level var is legal Go, so nothing but this test stands between the mistake and a caller parsing a human line

move the stale-draft deletes back above the write and a delete spends the run's ONLY chance to land the notes — measured on a permanent 503, the run burned the shipped 1s/4s/16s schedule, exited 4 and sent the PATCH zero times — and the mirror image returns with it: a failed write then leaves the strays already gone, so the run destroys state and lands nothing

convergence bookkeeping outranks the verdict again: a stale DRAFT GitHub will not delete turns a release whose notes ALREADY landed into exit 4, which release.yml's status gate reads before the verdict — so the repository stops shipping artefacts while its notes are correct, over state the next run re-derives and re-converges

the leniency is subordinate to a write that SUCCEEDED, and extending it to the none verdict — where the delete is the entire action — means a run that did nothing at all reports fine, leaving a residual draft standing for a release glyph has decided is not due

75 of the 83 breaking commits in the fleet take their breaking-ness ONLY from a retired Conventional token's ! — drop the line that lifts it out and nine in ten of them go quiet, so every repo whose unreleased range holds one cuts a smaller version than it owes, with no error and no change of its own
the struct half of the same decision: the ! survives into Commit.Breaking and into the canonical rewrite the violation hands the author, so a legacy breaking commit is still told to write one

the mention fence is Line's LAST pass over the assembled line and the only one left callable, so a String that returns its bytes unfenced turns every composed notes line and preview cell into a potential live @mention — a notification to a stranger (t-hykw), shipped fleet-wide
the release-notes golden holds fenced mentions on purpose; a Line that stops fencing rewrites shipped notes into ones that link and notify strangers, and this golden is the artifact-level witness

a create whose answer is lost goes back to replaying blind, and a draft has no tag for GitHub to collide on — so every replayed POST mints another identical draft, up to four siblings from one spent schedule for a human to pick through, and on an incomplete walk nothing ever converges them away

below: exists because at tag-push the new tag IS the highest v* tag — drop the strict bound and the resolver answers the tag being cut (an empty walk, so every release ships the placeholder body) or walks backwards from a higher tag, the silent-wrong-verdict class 012bfba killed in the binary

an awk over git tag --sort=v:refname answers the predecessor question with a refname sort, not a version order — a prerelease tag comes back as the base (released commits re-folded into the notes) or the predecessor comes back EMPTY (the job dies behind a tag that already exists), and no Go test can see a defect living in shell (t-s5n4)

the untagged arm is the one resolution with no tag to bound it and release.yml runs it on every push of a repository that has not released yet — drop the cap and a resolved --since-tag silently pays one API round-trip per commit of the WHOLE history (four fleet repositories measured walking everything on the v0.11.1 rollout), burning the Actions token budget on a walk nobody asked to be unbounded

a moving glyph ref inside the caller's composite action passes doctor — the consumer shape DESIGN §6 recommends escapes the one check whose header names that miss as its single unaffordable failure mode

blank the verdict's target and the dry run goes back to answering the same bytes for every --target — the preview stops naming the commit the eventual tag points at, so a typo'd sha first surfaces on the real write

the same goreleaser run has already pushed the new version to the tap, so a draft release is a window where `brew install` fetches a 404 asset until a human remembers to publish — cifail v0.1.1 sat broken for 17 days, and the revert is one word CI stays green over (1015774)

--retry 3's ~7s window measurably lost to a real GitHub outage (504x4, t-yj1b) and this action fronts every fleet repo's lint/pr-verdict/release — a shrunk width is invisible until an outage turns the whole fleet red at once (bcd93e3)

glyph notes exits 1 on an infra-only range by contract, and a bare invocation under set -e turns that verdict into a job abort behind a tag that already exists — no binaries, no cask, no attestation (7d8d733)

Go's -X ignores an unknown symbol with exit 0 and zero warnings (measured), so a moved package or renamed var ships every released binary reporting "dev" while build.yml's plain go build smoke is structurally blind to it

a SIGTERM landing in the hooks read is the operator aborting the run, and a guard that asks only the API read launders it into exit 4 with the abort rendered as commit-msg-hook could-not-run — the one code the fleet wrappers retry, so CI retries a run its operator stopped (the same signal in the API read exits 130 with nothing written)

a draft a human tagged vNext wears the v but is not the house shape, and without the ParseVersion arm the upsert adopts it — a none verdict DELETEs the human's work, a release verdict overwrites its tag and body with glyph's and files the rest as strays, and the same listing feeds the dry run, so the preview lies identically

a range that judged NO commit exits 0 exactly like a clean pass, so a stale base, an unfetched ref or an all-bot push reads as "every commit OK" — drop the verdict and the gate is back to reporting success over work it never looked at, which lint.yml only ever guarded for one cause and only on the caller side of the pin

a reusable job id is the second half of the check-run context 21 fleet repositories require on main (measured 2026-08-10, under two different caller halves), so renaming one never goes red here — the required context simply stops reporting and every one of those repositories blocks on a check that will never arrive

:construction: is legal mid-branch and illegal at the merge, so blocking it on a topic branch makes the branch unpushable and the only escape is --no-verify — the one that turns the whole gate off, traded for a rule the merge would have caught anyway

without the remote-tracking tips the range is the branch's whole history: every commit the remote has held for weeks is re-judged on every push, and on a repository with pre-glyph history that is a hook that can never be satisfied

git writes the null oid at the repository's object width, so a 40-char test reads a sha256 repository's DELETE as a real push of a commit that does not exist — an exit 4 on `git push --delete`, on the shape a width test looks obviously correct for

the pre-push script is installed once into ~34 clones and nothing refreshes one, so arithmetic put there goes on computing the OLD range in every repository forever — and a wrong range is a wrong verdict, not a loud failure

a commit the remote already holds on ANOTHER ref still arrives on the default branch when pushed there, and excluding every remote tip removed it from the range — measured against a real `git push`, a :construction: commit pushed to a topic branch first then to main was let through in silence by the one gate that exists to stop it

only a glyph-written hook whose bytes have MOVED is drift: a current hook and somebody else's standing choice must both stay silent, or the notice fires on every commit in every repository and becomes the noise that trains people to stop reading warnings

lint.yml no longer rebuilds per-finding annotations from the envelope — the binary is the ONLY writer of the ::error:: lines a reviewer acts on, so dropping this loop loses every per-commit pointer fleet-wide while the exit code, the envelope and the whole suite stay green

on a topic branch :construction: is legal by ratification (DESIGN §2), so a push arm without the default-branch guard reverses that decision repo-wide the day any caller widens its trigger — and it reverses it at the pin, in every repository at once

a refusal downgraded to exit 0 is the silent pass wearing a warning: ref creation has no base and a force push hides exactly the rewritten commits, so "linting" either range answers green over work never looked at — the defect class the push arm exists to close

default-branch history is immutable, so a gating verdict there is a red that can never be made green — the permanently red check trains the fleet to stop reading its own gate, which costs every OTHER verdict the gate ever renders

the title's destination is main — a squash merge records it as the landed subject — so judging it with the authoring-time tolerance blesses a :construction: title the WIP gate then meets only after it is history, where the annotate-only push arm can name it but nothing can stop it

a squash attributes the landed commit to the pull's author, so a bot's title is excluded exactly as a bot's commit is — judge it and every dependabot pull, a daily fleet-wide event whose titles are not the bot's to change, reds a gate whose code lint.yml forwards verbatim

the squash title is the one merge-candidate subject the BASE..HEAD range can never hold, and losing its step reds nothing — the range job stays green while 158 measured fleet subjects' worth of hole reopens, resurfacing only as silently dropped bumps in later release walks

a probe that sailed through at exit 0 is the whole finding — current bytes over a glyph that cannot answer, every commit on that machine going unlinted — and reporting it as pass restores exactly the confidently-wrong byte-compare verdict this check was built to break
same decision asserted end to end: doctor must exit 3 and annotate when the fired hook waves a violation through, or the one tool that can notice a dead local gate greets it with a green report

the probe must fire the byte-identical hook and ONLY that one — never firing leaves the check answering "nothing to fire" about a hook it should be exercising, and firing the other arms runs code a read-only diagnosis does not vouch for (a foreign hook is its owner's to run)

the fix key is the machine home of the suggestion — lose it and agents go back to regexing detail prose that PR #78 already reworded once, so the next rewording silently breaks every consumer the stable rule ids exist to protect

the invariant is Lint(Format(m)) empty or refuse — emit a best-effort line instead and the caller pipes output that still fails lint into git commit -F -, which is the exact three-round-trip loop fmt was built to end, now wearing the tool that promised to end it
same invariant at the command surface: a refusal is exit 3 with NOTHING on stdout, because a payload beside a warning exit code is a payload some pipeline consumes

measured on the fleet corpus, a quarter of uppercase subjects open with an all-caps word — lowercasing one rune mints "tOML", a wrong answer lint itself blesses, pasted with confidence; the mechanical fix must refuse where the repair is a rewording

an author who already wrote the footer is told to write the footer — the byte-identical answer PR #78 called two different mistakes sharing one sentence, and the wrap hazard it hides worst is the one that already misclassified a glyph commit as breaking when prose wrapped onto the magic word

a three-commit cleanup becomes three separate red runs, each revealing the next — the walk knows every unparsable commit before it fails and choosing to name one is pure withheld information, measured as an agent re-running lint in a loop over what bump had already seen

DESIGN has defined the subject as English since the scaffold and 592 fleet subjects drifted through while nothing held it — drop the one rule that does and the sentence goes back to being documentation, with the drift invisible until a release notes page renders in two languages
